questions.q: What term describes a substance made of two or more different elements chemically bonded together in a fixed ratio?
Which of the following characteristics is true for a physical mixture?
a: Its components can be separated easily by physical methods
It has a fixed chemical formula
Its properties are completely different from its ingredients

questions.q: What happens to the properties of elements when they chemically react to form a compound?
a: They change completely, forming a substance with new properties

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical compound rather than a mixture?
How can the components of an iron and sulfur mixture be easily separated without a chemical reaction?
a: Using a magnet to attract the iron
Heating them strongly until they melt together

questions.q: What is formed when iron powder and sulfur powder are heated strongly together until a chemical reaction takes place?
a: A mixture of iron and sulfur

questions.q: Which of the following represents a mixture rather than a pure chemical compound?
Why does a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gas behave differently than a molecule of water?
a: Water is a gas at room temperature
Water can be separated by a magnet
Hydrogen and oxygen in a mixture are not chemically bonded and retain their individual gas properties

questions.q: What type of change is involved when a chemical compound is formed from its elements?
Which statement best contrasts compounds and mixtures?
a: Compounds have variable composition while mixtures have fixed composition
Compounds have fixed chemical formulas and chemical bonding, whereas mixtures have variable composition and physical bonding
Both compounds and mixtures require chemical reactions to separate
Neither compounds nor mixtures have properties related to their elements

questions.q: When sulfur and iron react to form iron sulfide, what can be said about the mass of the products compared to the reactants?
a: Total mass remains exactly the same (conservation of mass)

questions.q: Which of these everyday materials is classified as a mixture?
a: Brass (an alloy of copper and zinc)

questions.q: Can the components of a chemical compound be separated by simple physical methods like filtration or magnetism?
a: No, chemical reactions or electrolysis are required
Yes, by leaving it in the sun

questions.q: What is formed when carbon burns completely in a sufficient supply of oxygen gas?
Which of the following substances cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical or physical means?
In a mixture of sand and salt dissolved in water, how do the individual substances behave?
a: They combine to form a new chemical compound
They react to produce heat and gas
They retain their individual chemical properties

questions.q: What term describes a mixture where substances are not evenly distributed throughout (like oil and water)?
What term describes a uniform mixture where components are completely blended on a microscopic level (like saltwater)?
Which of the following processes is required to separate the elements hydrogen and water from liquid water?
a: Electrolysis (passing an electric current through water)

questions.q: Why is air classified as a mixture rather than a compound?
a: It has a fixed chemical formula like A2
Its gases are chemically bonded together
It is always a liquid at room temperature
Its gases (nitrogen, oxygen, argon, etc.) can vary slightly in proportion and are not chemically bonded

questions.q: What happens to energy (heat or light) during the formation of many chemical compounds from elements?
a: Energy is often released or absorbed
Energy is turned into solid mass

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of a chemical compound?
a: It can be separated by sorting with tweezers
The elements combine in fixed, definite proportions by mass
Its boiling point varies depending on how much you mix
It looks identical to its starting elements

questions.q: If you mix 10 grams of iron filings and 10 grams of sulfur powder in a beaker without heating, what do you have?
a: A physical mixture of iron and sulfur

questions.q: Which separation technique is appropriate for separating a soluble solid compound from its liquid solution?
What is formed when a metal reacts chemically with oxygen?
Which of the following substances is a chemical compound containing hydrogen and oxygen?
a: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gases

questions.q: How do the melting points of pure compounds compare to mixtures?
a: Compounds melt over a wide range of temperatures
Pure compounds melt at a sharp, specific, fixed temperature
Mixtures always melt at higher temperatures than compounds

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the naming of simple binary compounds made from a metal and a non-metal?
a: The metal name is changed to end in -ide
The metal name comes first, and the non-metal name ends in -ide

questions.q: What is the chemical name for the compound formed when magnesium burns brightly in oxygen?
Which of the following best describes the composition of a chemical compound?
a: Variable proportions depending on the maker
Constant and fixed proportions of elements

questions.q: If sulfur burns in air, it forms sulfur dioxide. Is sulfur dioxide an element, a mixture, or a compound?
Which statement is incorrect when comparing mixtures and compounds?
a: Compounds have chemical bonds between atoms
Mixtures can be separated by physical methods
Compounds retain the exact physical properties of their constituent elements
Mixtures do not have fixed chemical formulas

questions.q: What is formed when hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate?
a: A chemical reaction producing a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas
A simple physical mixture of rock and acid
An unreactive mixture with no changes

questions.q: Why is petroleum (crude oil) considered a mixture rather than a compound?
a: It is a mixture of different hydrocarbons that can be separated by physical fractional distillation
It has a single fixed boiling point
It is made of only one element

questions.q: When table salt (sodium chloride) is dissolved in water to form saltwater, what kind of system has been created?
Which of the following methods would successfully separate a mixture of iron filings and sand?
a: Using a magnet to attract the iron filings

questions.q: What happens to the individual atoms of elements when they form a compound?
a: They join together through chemical bonding

questions.q: Which of the following is a compound formed from sodium and chlorine?
In a laboratory experiment, hydrogen and oxygen are mixed in a test tube. No spark is applied. What is inside the test tube?
a: A physical mixture of two gases

questions.q: Which of the following describes a key difference in how properties are exhibited?
a: Compounds show the properties of their elements
Mixtures lose all properties of their ingredients
Mixtures retain the properties of the individual substances that make them up
